q: Does the epsilon^(2q+1) identity of Eq. (6) remain EXACT (not merely approximate) when the source-preparation unitary U is a generic Haar-random unitary rather than the H^{\otimes n} we tested, for the same effective epsilon = 1 - |U_{ts}|^2?
basis: Our verification used U = H^{\otimes n} exclusively (12/12 cells matched to ~1e-15). The paper writes Eq. (6) for arbitrary U but does not visibly quantify sensitivity of the identity to the choice of U. It is not obvious whether the exact identity relies on the highly structured Hadamard source or is a genuinely U-independent statement.
next_steps: Reuse tulsi_grover_patel_fixed_point.py: replace U with a QR-decomposed random unitary drawn from the Haar measure at n=3,4; hold epsilon fixed by rescaling; sweep q=1..6; measure max |measured - epsilon^(2q+1)| across 100 random U samples per (n,q). If any random U produces a non-machine-precision gap, characterise which structural property of U it violates.

q: How large, quantitatively, is the average-case query-count advantage of the two-ancilla algorithm over Phase-pi/3 as a function of the prior distribution over epsilon?
basis: The paper claims strictly-better average-case performance than Phase-pi/3 but leaves the size of that gain qualitative. Our replication only exercised worst-case (deterministic residual error at a fixed epsilon).
next_steps: Add a matching numpy simulator for Phase-pi/3, define 'success' as residual error <= 1e-3, and compute E[queries] under three priors on epsilon: uniform on (0,1), Beta(2,2) (mildly peaked), and a power-law prior epsilon^-1 (small-epsilon-heavy). Report the ratio E[queries_TGP] / E[queries_phase-pi/3] for each prior.

q: At what per-gate depolarizing (or amplitude-damping) noise level does the epsilon^(2q+1) fixed-point property break down, and how does the breakdown depth scale with the noise strength p?
basis: The paper's Feature (2) informally claims 'any errors due to imperfect transformations in earlier iterations are wiped out by the subsequent iterations,' but this is asserted qualitatively; our ideal-simulator replication cannot bound how far that self-correction extends.
next_steps: Convert the statevector simulator into a density-matrix simulator, apply a depolarizing channel of strength p after each oracle and diffusion, and measure residual error at q=1..10 for p in {1e-4, 1e-3, 1e-2}. Fit the residual error as a function of (q, p) and identify the crossover q*(p) beyond which the noise-driven floor exceeds epsilon^(2q+1).

q: Is the second ancilla strictly necessary? Can a one-ancilla algorithm with an adaptive (measurement-outcome-dependent) diffusion choice achieve the same epsilon^(2q+1) optimum for all positive integer q?
basis: The paper motivates the second ancilla solely to cap f <= 1/2 so the simple sub-algorithm's regime of dominance is entered. That is an existence argument, not a lower bound on the number of ancillas needed.
next_steps: Enumerate one-ancilla circuits parameterised by a single mid-circuit measurement and a small family of adaptive diffusion angles; brute-force search at n=2, q in {1,2,3} for any parameter setting that reproduces epsilon^(2q+1) to machine precision. If any is found, publish; if none, formalize as a two-ancilla lower bound conjecture.

q: In our replication the absolute error |measured - epsilon^(2q+1)| grew roughly linearly in q, from ~3e-16 at q=1 to ~3e-15 at q=4, despite each iteration involving a re-normalisation that could in principle amplify unit roundoff multiplicatively. What is the true numerical-stability scaling of this algorithm and does it agree with an a priori bound?
basis: Data in results.json shows monotone but sub-multiplicative error growth in q. This is a positive observation but was not predicted (we conservatively expected worse), and deserves an analytical explanation.
next_steps: Push q to 20 at n=2 (still trivially cheap), record |Delta|(q); fit log|Delta| vs q with slope test. Cross-check against a Higham-style backward-error analysis of a reflection-followed-by-projection composition; identify whether the observed linearity comes from unitary contractivity of the diffusion reflection or from cancellation in the projector.
